interpretation: D improves handwriting most but fails positive-edge and long-sequence absolute regression gates. C epoch 1 passes the fixed numerical gates, but ties frozen E1 plus contrast B on space-sensitive CER (62 errors), has zero exact tiers versus B one, and has slightly worse clean/positive/long regression. Its one-error no-whitespace advantage over B is not convincing evidence that replacing E1 weights is worthwhile on one writer/two sources. Keep the gate-passing C checkpoint for further controlled development review, without changing the operational selected-model file. B is an exploratory normalization-only option; no deployment/rejection-policy claim.
